<explanation>
Based on the complete file tree and the README content, Xournal++ is clearly an open‐source C++ application for digital note taking. It is a desktop application (with experimental mobile port support) that relies on a layered architecture with a clear separation between the GUI, business logic, data models, file handling (including reading and writing its specific file formats), and extension points such as plugins. Here’s how you can design a detailed system design diagram that accurately represents the architecture of Xournal++:

1. Identify the Main Components:
   • GUI / Presentation Layer – The user interface is built using GTK (with Glade XML files), which includes various dialogs (e.g., settings, export, plugin configuration), toolbars, menus, and sidebar components.
   • Core / Control Layer – This layer handles event management, input devices (e.g., pen, mouse, touch), tool controllers, file loading/saving and undo/redo functionalities. Look in folders like src/core/control, src/core/gui, src/core/undo, and src/core/view.
   • Model Layer – This component represents the document model (pages, layers, strokes, elements) and the business data behind note-taking; it is located in modules under src/core/model.
   • PDF and Export Modules – This includes PDF export functionality, background handling, and file format management (with .xopp and .xoj support). Components are in folders such as src/core/pdf.
   • Plugin Framework – Xournal++ supports plugins (written in Lua) to extend its capabilities. The plugins directory (and related parts in src/core/plugin) shows where these integration points are.
   • Utilities & Helpers – Shared classes and functions found under src/util for tasks like logging, assertions, string manipulation, and serializing.
   • Platform/Build and Deployment – There is a significant amount of supporting infrastructure for cross-platform builds (directories like windows-setup, mac-setup, linux-setup, and CI configuration in .github and cmake files) that indicates how the project is built, tested, and deployed.

2. Determining Relationships and Interactions:
   • Clearly show that the GUI layer interacts with the Control layer (input handling, dialogs, toolbars, menus) by sending user events that the control modules process.
   • The Control layer then routes operations to the Model layer (for document manipulation, undo/redo, and changes in stroke or layout).
   • The Model layer’s state is rendered back in the GUI via the View components (also found in src/core/view).
   • The PDF processing, export, and attachment management are intermediate services that connect with both the Model (for data extraction) and the GUI (for display and export commands).
   • The Plugin framework is an extension module that integrates with the Control and Model layers through clearly defined APIs; illustrate it as a side block that connects with the main application flow.

3. Highlight Architectural Patterns and Design Principles:
   • Layered (or MVC-like) Architecture is evident: UI (view), control (event handling/tool management) and data models (document structure). Emphasize the separation between these concerns.
   • Extensibility through plugins is a core design principle – show the plugin interface as a well-defined extension point.
   • Dependency management and configuration via CMake and various CI pipelines (GitHub Actions, workflows for different platforms) are also part of the overall system structure.
   • Cross-platform support is built into the project through platform-specific directories and build configurations.

4. Include Relevant Technologies and Frameworks:
   • C++ as the principal programming language.
   • GTK and Glade for the graphical user interface.
   • CMake for build configuration.
   • Lua for plugin support.
   • Various CI/CD tooling indicated by GitHub workflows.
   • External libraries for PDF exports, audio handling, and possibly others (as seen from the presence of multiple components in the core modules).

5. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:
   • Since this is an open-source desktop application serving as a note-taking tool (with support for PDF annotation, stylus input, and multimedia elements), separate the diagram into clearly distinct layers or modules.
   • Use distinct shapes or colors—for example, use one color for UI components, another for control/logic modules, and a third for data models. You might also use a different shape (like a cylinder for database or file storage) for the file format handling and export modules.
   • Clearly label each block (e.g., “GUI – MainWindow, Dialogs, Toolbars”, “Control – Input Managers, Undo/Redo, Job Scheduling”, “Model – Document, Pages, Layers, Strokes”, “Export – PDF Export, Image Export”, “Plugins – Lua Scripting Engine”) and denote how they interact.
   • Use directional arrows to show data flow: from user events in the GUI to the control layer, then updates in the model, and back to the GUI, as well as connections to the export and plugin subsystems.
   • Indicate external integration points such as CI/CD components (GitHub Actions, packaging scripts) separately, showing they influence the build and deployment process.

6. Recommended Diagram Elements:
   • Create nodes for each major component (e.g., GUI, Control, Model, Export, Plugin framework, Build/CI Infrastructure).
   • Mark dependencies with directional arrows (e.g., “User Input” arrow from GUI to Control; “Updates” arrow from Control to Model; “Render/Refresh” arrow from Model to GUI).
   • Use icons or labels to denote platform-specific support (e.g., Windows, Mac, Linux) where appropriate.
   • Consider secondary nodes (such as Utilities) that support multiple layers.
   • Optionally include a section that shows build configuration and continuous integration pipelines that trigger tests, builds, and packaging for different platforms.

By following these guidelines and ensuring that your diagram reflects both the layered architecture (from presentation to control to data models) and highlights the extensibility points (plugins, cross-platform builds), you will create a well-detailed, accurate, and effective system design diagram that matches the Xournal++ project’s structure and purpose.
</explanation>
